nodes.label: License Controller
nodes.rationale: Decides what is allowed (allocation, leases, policy, reconciliation, audit) across an org-wide pool of core entitlements.

nodes.label: KMS Host (Activation Authority)
nodes.rationale: Decides what is activated via Volume Activation Services role with customer CSVLK. Configured, not built.

nodes.label: Hypervisor / Cloud Platform
nodes.rationale: Decides what is actually running; independent private cloud infrastructure exposing VM power-state / control-plane API.

nodes.label: Tripartite Authority Principle
nodes.rationale: License Controller decides what is allowed; KMS decides what is activated; Hypervisor decides what is actually running. None must stand in for another.

nodes.label: Flexible Virtualization Benefit (FVB)
nodes.rationale: Microsoft licensing foundation enabling dynamic core allocation to Windows Server Standard VMs on authorized non-listed infrastructure.

nodes.label: FVB Legal Eligibility Conditions
nodes.rationale: Requires active SA/subscription, non-Listed Provider host, same server farm, 8-core minimum per VM, 16-core customer floor.

nodes.label: Written Microsoft / Reseller Confirmation
nodes.rationale: Highest-priority open action: legal confirmation must be obtained in writing before production reliance.

nodes.label: VM Agent
nodes.rationale: Windows Service on target VMs. Connects outbound-only to controller, heartbeats, caches locally, queries activation without touching license keys.

nodes.label: Windows Server 2025 Standard VM
nodes.rationale: Standardized target OS edition with 8-core minimum allocation, KMS GVLK configured.

nodes.label: Outbound HTTPS / mTLS Transport
nodes.rationale: Agent-initiated outbound-only transport; requires no open inbound ports on guest VMs.

nodes.label: Tier 1: Pre-Boot Admission Control
nodes.rationale: Preferred enforcement mechanism: controller gates platform VM start requests directly, ensuring true prevention.

nodes.label: Tier 2: Platform RBAC Gating
nodes.rationale: Practical fallback: platform VM start rights restricted to controller service account; human starts route via controller.

nodes.label: Tier 3: Detection & Alerting
nodes.rationale: Minimum viable stopgap: reconciliation detects unauthorized running VM within minutes and fires alerts.

nodes.label: VM State Detection Model
nodes.rationale: Six discrete states (RUNNING, STOPPING, STOPPED, TERMINATED, UNREACHABLE, UNKNOWN) governing lease reservation and release.

nodes.label: Unreachable State Policy
nodes.rationale: Strict policy: heartbeat loss without authoritative hypervisor confirmation does NOT auto-release, preventing over-allocation during network disconnects.

nodes.label: Controller API (FastAPI)
nodes.rationale: FastAPI service exposing idempotent endpoints for allocation, lease management, and policy enforcement.

nodes.label: Reconciliation Engine
nodes.rationale: First-class background subsystem comparing expected leases vs actual hypervisor running state on schedule.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL State Store
nodes.rationale: Relational state backend using SQLAlchemy + Alembic, storing entitlements, vms, leases, and audit_log.

nodes.label: Append-Only Audit Log
nodes.rationale: Immutable compliance trail recording all allocate, release, reconciliation, and enforcement events with timestamp and actor.

nodes.label: Management Dashboard (React)
nodes.rationale: React + REST UI for monitoring capacity; strictly off the licensing-critical execution path.

nodes.label: Idempotent Request Key (request_id)
nodes.rationale: Client-supplied unique request key ensuring retried network requests cannot allocate duplicate core seats.

nodes.label: Hypervisor UUID (Immutable Identity)
nodes.rationale: Hardware/platform UUID preventing cloned or renamed VMs from impersonating legitimate allocated machines.

nodes.label: Scale-Appropriate Descoping
nodes.rationale: Deliberately excludes multi-controller HA, snapshot fencing tokens, and combinatorial failure matrices for 10-VM scale.

nodes.label: Explicit Scope Boundaries
nodes.rationale: RDS CALs (perpetual), VDA E3 per-user licensing, and routine guest slmgr /upk deactivation are explicitly excluded.
